title: Sun Beams Over Kitt Peak
caption: Sunlight over the Mayall Telescope, Kitt Peak National Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Light from the Sun breaks over a craggy ridge, leaving the upper parts of several telescope domes and the 4-meter Nicholas U. Mayall Telescope in silhouette. The ridge is part of Kitt Peak National Observatory, run as a Program of NSF NOIRLab, which sits in southern Arizona at an altitude of 2096 meters (6877 feet).

Kitt Peak hosts more than 20 telescopes, used both for astronomy at night and for studying the Sun by day. According to NOIRLab, that makes it one of the biggest gatherings of astronomical instruments north of the equator.

The Mayall Telescope, eighteen stories tall, rises above the ridge and stands out on the Kitt Peak skyline. It is the biggest telescope on Kitt Peak, and the tower and dome can be spotted from more than 80 kilometers (50 miles) away.
